questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: Which of the following is a root that we eat as a vegetable?
questions.explanation: A carrot is the swollen root of the carrot plant. Spinach is a leaf, cauliflower is a flower and peas are seeds.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: Honey is a food that we get from which animal?
questions.explanation: Honeybees collect nectar from flowers and make honey in their hives.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: An animal that eats only plants is called a
questions.explanation: Herbivores such as cows and goats feed only on plants and plant products.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: Which group contains only foods that come from animals?
questions.explanation: Egg, honey and milk are all animal products. The other groups include plant foods such as wheat, rice or potato.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: A student eats a salad containing tomato slices, spinach leaves and sprouted moong. Which plant parts is the student eating?
questions.explanation: Tomato is a fruit, spinach is a leaf and sprouted moong are germinating seeds.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: Which of these animals is an omnivore?
questions.explanation: A crow eats both plant matter such as grains and animal matter such as insects and meat scraps.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: All food that we eat can be traced back to plants in some way. Which reasoning best supports this statement?
options: Plants make milk and eggs directly
Animals such as cows and hens depend on plants for their own food, so milk and eggs come indirectly from plants
questions.explanation: Cows eat grass and hens eat grains, so the milk and eggs they give depend on plants.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: A farmer finds that a field of wheat has been eaten by deer, and a hunter later kills the deer for meat. Which sequence shows the correct flow of food?
questions.explanation: The wheat plant is eaten by the deer and the deer is eaten by the hunter, so food moves from wheat to deer to hunter.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: Give three examples of foods we get from plants, each from a different plant part, and name the part.
questions.answer: Carrot is a root, spinach is a leaf and mango is a fruit.
keyPoints: Each example correctly matched to its part
questions.explanation: Plants give us food from roots, stems, leaves, flowers, fruits and seeds.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: Explain the difference between a herbivore, a carnivore and an omnivore with one example of each.
questions.answer: A herbivore eats only plants (cow), a carnivore eats only other animals (lion) and an omnivore eats both plants and animals (crow or human).
questions.explanation: Animals are classified by what they eat.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which nutrient is called the body-building nutrient?
questions.explanation: Proteins help the body to grow and repair damaged cells.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The deficiency of which mineral causes a swelling in the neck called goitre?
questions.explanation: Lack of iodine in the diet causes goitre.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which chemical is used to test for the presence of starch in food?
questions.explanation: Iodine solution turns blue-black when it touches starch.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A drop of dilute iodine solution is put on a boiled potato slice and it turns blue-black. What does this show?
questions.explanation: A blue-black colour with iodine is the test result for starch, a carbohydrate.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Rickets, in which bones become soft and bent, is caused by lack of
questions.explanation: Vitamin D helps the body to use calcium for strong bones; it is made in the skin in sunlight.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is roughage important in our diet even though it gives no nutrients?
options: It gives a lot of energy
It helps the body to get rid of undigested food
questions.explanation: Roughage, or dietary fibre, helps in removing waste from the body.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A child eats only rice and potatoes every day. Which problem is most likely to occur over a long time?
options: Lack of proteins and vitamins, leading to deficiency
questions.explanation: Rice and potato are mainly carbohydrates, so the diet lacks proteins, vitamins and minerals and is not balanced.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A person who lives indoors and rarely goes into sunlight is more likely to have weak bones. What is the best explanation?
options: The body makes vitamin D in sunlight, and this helps bones
questions.explanation: The skin makes vitamin D when exposed to sunlight, and vitamin D helps bones use calcium.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is a balanced diet? Why should it include fruits and vegetables?
questions.answer: A balanced diet has all the nutrients in the right amounts. Fruits and vegetables supply vitamins, minerals and roughage.
keyPoints: Fruits and vegetables give vitamins and minerals
questions.explanation: A balanced diet keeps the body healthy and prevents deficiency diseases.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Describe how you would test whether a piece of paper that was rubbed with a food item contains fat.
questions.answer: Rub the food on a piece of paper and let it dry. If an oily patch that lets light pass through remains, the food contains fat.
questions.explanation: Fats leave a translucent oily stain on paper.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Cotton fibre is obtained from which part of the cotton plant?
questions.explanation: Cotton fibres grow in the fruit of the plant called the cotton boll.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which fibre is obtained from the stem of a plant?
questions.explanation: Jute fibre is obtained from the stem of the jute plant.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The process of making yarn from fibres is called
questions.explanation: In spinning, fibres are drawn out and twisted to form yarn.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Combing cotton to separate seeds from the fibres is called
questions.explanation: The process of separating cotton fibres from seeds is called ginning.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Silk fibre is obtained from the
questions.explanation: The silkworm spins a cocoon of silk fibre, which is collected and processed.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Yarn is made into fabric by
questions.explanation: Fabrics are made from yarn by weaving on looms or by knitting.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A cotton shirt is comfortable in summer but a woollen sweater is worn in winter. Which statement best explains why?
options: Wool absorbs sweat and cotton traps air
Cotton absorbs sweat and lets it dry, while wool traps air and keeps the body warm
questions.explanation: Cotton absorbs sweat, which helps in hot weather, while wool traps air between its fibres and slows heat loss.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: After a sheep is shorn, the wool is not directly turned into yarn. Which step must come first?
options: Cleaning it and removing dirt and grease
questions.explanation: Raw wool is cleaned, sorted and scoured before it is spun into yarn.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Name two animals from which wool is obtained, and two uses of wool.
questions.answer: Sheep and goat give wool, which is used to make sweaters and shawls.
keyPoints: Two correct animals such as sheep, goat, yak or camel
Two uses such as sweaters and blankets
questions.explanation: Wool comes from the hair of animals such as sheep, goat and yak.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Describe the steps that turn raw cotton into a cotton shirt.
questions.answer: Cotton is picked and ginned to remove seeds, spun into yarn, woven or knitted into cloth, and then cut and stitched.
questions.explanation: Fibre to yarn to fabric to garment is the usual order.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of these materials is transparent?
questions.explanation: Clear glass lets light pass through, so we can see clearly through it.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The shine on the surface of metals is called
questions.explanation: Lustre is the shining appearance of the surface of a material such as a metal.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of these dissolves in water?
questions.explanation: Sugar is soluble in water. The others do not dissolve.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Through an oiled sheet of paper you can see objects, but not clearly. This paper is
questions.explanation: Translucent materials allow some light through, so objects look blurred.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which pair contains one object that sinks and one that floats in water?
questions.explanation: An iron nail sinks, while a cork floats.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Water and mustard oil, when mixed and left alone, form two layers. This shows that oil is
options: Insoluble and does not mix with water
questions.explanation: Oil does not mix with water, so the two liquids stay in separate layers.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A window of a bathroom is made of frosted glass. Why is it chosen rather than clear glass?
options: It is opaque and lets in no light
It is translucent, letting in light but preventing clear view from outside
questions.explanation: Frosted glass lets light through but blurs the view, giving privacy.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A cooking pan has a metal body and a plastic handle. Which reason best explains the choice of handle?
options: Plastic does not let heat pass through easily, so the handle stays cool to hold
questions.explanation: Plastic is a poor conductor of heat, so the handle does not get very hot.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Define transparent, translucent and opaque materials and give an example of each.
questions.answer: Transparent materials let light pass so that we can see clearly through them (glass). Translucent materials let some light pass (butter paper). Opaque materials let no light pass (wood).
questions.explanation: The classification depends on how much light passes through a material.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A stone, a cork, an iron nail and a wooden spoon are placed in water. Which will sink and which will float? What does this tell us about materials?
questions.answer: The stone and iron nail sink; the cork and wooden spoon float. Some materials are heavier for their size than water and sink, others float.
keyPoints: Materials differ in whether they sink or float
questions.explanation: Floating and sinking is a property used to group materials.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Separating grains from their stalks is called
questions.explanation: Threshing is the process of separating grains from the harvested stalks.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Winnowing is used to separate
options: Heavier and lighter components of a mixture using wind
questions.explanation: In winnowing, wind blows away lighter husk while heavier grains fall nearby.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Common salt is obtained from sea water by
questions.explanation: Sea water is left in shallow pans; the sun evaporates the water and leaves the salt.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which method can separate wheat flour from larger pieces of bran?
questions.explanation: A sieve lets fine flour pass but holds back larger bran pieces.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Muddy water is left to stand and the soil settles at the bottom. Pouring out the clear water without disturbing the soil is called
questions.explanation: Settling of heavy particles is sedimentation, and pouring off the clear liquid is decantation.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A mixture of sand and iron filings can easily be separated using
questions.explanation: A magnet attracts iron filings but not sand.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A student dissolves salt in water and then tries to separate it by filtering through filter paper. Why does the salt not get separated?
options: Dissolved salt particles are too small and pass through the paper along with the water
questions.explanation: Dissolved salt passes through the pores of the filter paper. Evaporation is needed to recover it.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In a tea strainer, tea leaves are held back while the liquid tea passes through. Which separation idea is this most like?
questions.explanation: The strainer works like a sieve, holding back larger solid leaves while the liquid passes.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Explain how you would separate a mixture of sand, salt and water to get all three back.
questions.answer: Filter the mixture to remove sand. Heat the filtrate to evaporate the water and leave salt. The water vapour can be cooled to collect pure water.
questions.explanation: Different methods are combined to separate each component.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is winnowing done on a windy day and not on a still day?
questions.answer: Wind is needed to blow away the lighter husk while heavier grains fall down. Without wind the two would not separate.
questions.explanation: Winnowing depends on the difference in weight of the components.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of these is a reversible change?
questions.explanation: Water that melts from ice can be frozen back into ice.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which change cannot be reversed?
options: Melting butter and then cooling it
questions.explanation: Wax burnt in a flame turns into new substances and cannot be recovered.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Rusting of an iron nail needs
questions.explanation: Iron rusts when it is exposed to both oxygen in air and water.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of these is an irreversible change?
options: Dissolving sugar in water and evaporating it
questions.explanation: A baked cake cannot be turned back into batter.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why does a metal lid sometimes become easier to unscrew when held under hot water?
questions.explanation: Metals expand on heating and the lid becomes slightly loose.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A fruit ripens and its taste changes. This kind of change is
questions.explanation: A ripened fruit cannot become raw again.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A student leaves two iron nails: one in a dry sealed bottle and one in a bottle of water open to the air. After some days only the second rusts. What does this show?
options: Rusting happens in the dark only
Rusting needs both water and air
questions.explanation: The second nail had both water and air, while the first had none of water, so only the second rusted.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which statement correctly describes a change of state such as melting?
options: No new substance is formed and it can usually be reversed by cooling
New substances are formed and it cannot be reversed
questions.explanation: Melting changes the state of a substance but the substance remains the same, so cooling can reverse it.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Give two examples each of changes that can be reversed and changes that cannot be reversed.
questions.answer: Reversible: melting of ice, folding paper. Irreversible: burning wood, cooking an egg.
questions.explanation: A change that can be undone is reversible.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why should iron gates be painted regularly? Give a reason using the idea of changes.
questions.answer: Paint keeps air and water from touching the iron, so rusting, an irreversible change that weakens iron, is prevented.
questions.explanation: Preventing rust keeps the iron strong.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which part of the plant absorbs water from the soil?
questions.explanation: Roots take in water and minerals from the soil.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Plants that are small with soft, green stems are called
questions.explanation: Herbs have soft stems and are usually small.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The process by which green leaves make food is called
questions.explanation: In photosynthesis, leaves use sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to make food.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A plant has leaves with parallel veins. Its roots are most likely
questions.explanation: Plants with parallel venation, such as grass and wheat, usually have fibrous roots.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The female part of a flower is the
questions.explanation: The pistil is the female reproductive part; the stamen is the male part.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Water given out by leaves through tiny pores in the form of vapour is called
questions.explanation: Loss of water vapour from leaves is called transpiration.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A plant kept in a dark cupboard for many days becomes pale and weak. What is the best explanation?
options: The leaves could not make food without sunlight
questions.explanation: Without light, photosynthesis cannot take place, so the plant cannot make enough food.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: If a stem of white flower is placed in coloured water, the flower slowly takes up colour. What does this show?
options: Stems carry water upward to other parts
questions.explanation: The stem has tubes that carry water to leaves and flowers.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Name the main parts of a flower and mention the function of the petals.
questions.answer: A flower has sepals, petals, stamens and pistil. Petals are usually brightly coloured and attract insects.
questions.explanation: The stamen and pistil are the reproductive parts.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State the function of the stem and explain why a plant would fall down if its stem is cut.
questions.answer: The stem holds the plant upright and carries water and minerals to leaves and food to other parts. If it is cut, the plant is no longer supported and its parts lose water.
keyPoints: Cut stem breaks both support and transport
questions.explanation: The stem connects roots to leaves and supports the plant.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The joint at the shoulder is a
questions.explanation: At the shoulder, the round end of one bone fits into a cup-like space of another, allowing movement in all directions.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which part of the body protects the brain?
questions.explanation: The skull is a bony box that protects the brain.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The rib cage protects the
questions.explanation: The ribs, joined to the chest bone and backbone, enclose and protect the heart and lungs.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The knee and the elbow are examples of
questions.explanation: Hinge joints allow movement in only one direction, like a door hinge.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which animal moves with the help of a muscular foot?
questions.explanation: A snail glides along on its muscular foot.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The bones of the skull are joined by
questions.explanation: Most bones of the skull do not move and are joined by fixed joints.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: You can turn your head up, down and side to side but not roll your arm in the same way. Which is the best explanation?
options: The neck has a hinge joint
The neck has a pivotal joint that lets the head turn, while the shoulder has a different joint
questions.explanation: A pivotal joint at the neck allows the head to turn from side to side.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A bird's bones are light and hollow. Why is this useful?
options: It helps the bird to fly
questions.explanation: Light bones reduce the body weight, making flight easier.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Explain how the biceps and triceps muscles help us to bend and straighten the arm.
questions.answer: Muscles work in pairs. When the biceps contracts, the arm bends and the triceps relaxes. When the triceps contracts, the arm straightens and the biceps relaxes.
keyPoints: One contracts while the other relaxes
questions.explanation: Muscles can only pull, so a pair is needed to move a bone both ways.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why would a person with no joints be unable to walk, even if bones and muscles were present?
questions.answer: Joints allow bones to move relative to each other. Without them the bones would be rigid and the legs could not bend at the hip, knee or ankle.
questions.explanation: Walking needs joints, bones and muscles together.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The place where an organism lives is called its
questions.explanation: A habitat is the surrounding where a plant or animal normally lives.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of these is a non-living (abiotic) component of a habitat?
questions.explanation: Soil, water, air and rocks are abiotic components.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The special features that help an organism live in its habitat are called
questions.explanation: Adaptations are features or habits that help an organism survive in its surroundings.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which feature helps a fish to live in water?
questions.explanation: A streamlined body helps a fish swim and its gills let it breathe in water.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Leaves of a cactus are reduced to spines. This helps the plant to
options: Lose less water in the desert
questions.explanation: Spines reduce water loss, and the green stem carries out photosynthesis.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of all living things?
options: They respond to changes around them
They can move from place to place
questions.explanation: All living things respond to stimuli. Plants do not move from place to place and many animals have no bones.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Trees in mountain regions are often cone-shaped with sloping branches. How does this shape help them?
options: It makes them absorb more salt
It lets snow slide off easily
questions.explanation: The sloping branches let snow slide off, so the branches do not break under its weight.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A desert rat spends the day in a burrow and comes out at night. How does this help it?
options: It avoids the heat of the day and saves water
questions.explanation: Burrows are cooler during the day, which helps animals save water.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: List any four characteristics of living things.
questions.answer: Living things need food, respire, grow, respond to stimuli, reproduce and give out waste.
keyPoints: Food, breathing, growth, response, reproduction, excretion
questions.explanation: These features separate living things from non-living things.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A frog can live on land and in water. Explain how it is suited to both.
questions.answer: A frog has webbed feet for swimming and strong hind legs for jumping on land. It breathes through lungs on land and through its skin in water.
questions.explanation: Adaptations suit it to both habitats.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A car moving along a straight road shows
questions.explanation: Motion along a straight line is called rectilinear motion.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How can the length of a curved line be measured with a ruler?
options: Use a thread laid along the line, then straighten it and measure
questions.explanation: A thread can follow the curve; when straightened, its length can be read on the ruler.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The spinning of a top on the ground is an example of
questions.explanation: When an object turns about its own axis, the motion is rotational.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Two students measure the same table using their hand-spans and get different values. What does this show?
options: Body-part measurements are not standard and vary from person to person
questions.explanation: Different people have different hand-spans, so standard units are needed.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: While measuring a pencil with a ruler, the eye should be placed
options: Directly above the point being read
To the left of the mark
questions.explanation: Looking from directly above avoids a reading error caused by a slanted view.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Convert 3.5 km into metres and 250 cm into metres. Show your working.
questions.answer: 3.5 km x 1000 = 3500 m, and 250 cm divided by 100 = 2.5 m.
questions.explanation: Multiply to convert km to m and divide to convert cm to m.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Describe the different kinds of motion of the blades of a ceiling fan and of a child on a straight slide.
questions.answer: The fan blades show rotational motion about a fixed axis. The child on a straight slide shows rectilinear motion along a straight line.
questions.explanation: Motion is classified by the path followed.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of these objects is luminous?
questions.explanation: Luminous objects give out their own light, like a candle flame.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Light travels in
questions.explanation: Light travels in straight lines, which is why we get sharp shadows.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A shadow is formed when light is blocked by an
questions.explanation: Opaque objects do not allow light to pass, and a dark region forms behind them.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: An image formed by a pinhole camera is
questions.explanation: Light rays cross at the pinhole, so the image on the screen is upside down.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which is not needed to form a shadow?
questions.explanation: A shadow needs a light source, an opaque object and a screen.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The image in a plane mirror is
options: Same size as the object and behind the mirror
questions.explanation: A plane mirror gives an image of the same size that appears behind the mirror.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A boy moves his toy closer to a torch while the torch is fixed and a wall is behind it. What happens to the size of the shadow on the wall?
questions.explanation: The nearer an object is to the light source, the larger its shadow.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why can we see the Moon even though it does not produce its own light?
questions.explanation: The Moon is a non-luminous object that reflects the Sun's light.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why does the word AMBULANCE appear written backwards on the front of an ambulance?
questions.answer: The drivers ahead see it in their rear-view mirror, which reverses left and right, so the word looks correct in the mirror.
keyPoints: Mirror reflection reverses left and right
Words appear readable in rear-view mirror
questions.explanation: This is lateral inversion in a plane mirror.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Explain why a pinhole camera works only if the hole is small and the object is well lit.
questions.answer: A small hole limits light so that each point of the object forms a small spot and the image is sharp. Good lighting keeps the image bright.
keyPoints: Small hole gives a sharp image
questions.explanation: Straight-line travel of light underlies the pinhole camera.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The thin wire inside a bulb that glows is called the
questions.explanation: The filament heats up and gives light when current passes.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of these is a good conductor of electricity?
questions.explanation: Metals such as copper allow electric current to pass.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A device used to open or close an electric circuit is a
questions.explanation: A switch breaks or completes the circuit.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A bulb does not light even though it is connected to a cell by wires. A likely cause is
options: The circuit is open or broken
questions.explanation: Current flows only in a closed circuit, so a break stops the current.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which material is an insulator?
questions.explanation: Rubber does not let current pass easily.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A group of two or more cells connected together is called a
questions.explanation: Cells joined together form a battery.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A student tests a bottle cap, a coin, a pencil lead (graphite) and a rubber band in a circuit tester. Which will probably make the bulb glow?
questions.explanation: The metal coin and graphite conduct electricity, while rubber and plastic do not.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why are electrical wires covered with plastic or rubber?
options: Insulation prevents shocks and short circuits
questions.explanation: Insulating covers stop current from passing to the person who touches them.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why should we never touch electric switches with wet hands?
questions.answer: Water that has salts in it conducts electricity, so wet hands may let current pass through the body and give a shock.
questions.explanation: Safety around electricity is important.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Draw in words a simple circuit that lights a bulb, and say what happens when the switch is opened.
questions.answer: Connect a cell, switch and bulb in a loop with wires. When the switch is closed, current flows and the bulb glows. When it is opened the loop is broken and the bulb goes off.
keyPoints: Cell, switch, bulb and wires in a loop
questions.explanation: A complete path is needed for current.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of these is attracted by a magnet?
questions.explanation: Iron is a magnetic material.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The ends of a bar magnet are called
questions.explanation: Each magnet has a north pole and a south pole at its ends.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Like poles of two magnets
questions.explanation: North repels north and south repels south.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A freely hanging bar magnet comes to rest pointing in the
questions.explanation: A freely suspended magnet aligns itself roughly along north and south.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A magnetic compass is used to
questions.explanation: The needle of a compass is a small magnet pointing north-south.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which group contains only magnetic materials?
questions.explanation: Iron, nickel and cobalt are attracted by magnets.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: If a bar magnet is broken into two pieces, what happens?
options: One piece has only a north pole
Both lose their magnetism and become non-magnetic
The pieces repel and become heavy
Each piece becomes a magnet with two poles
questions.explanation: Each piece has its own north and south pole.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A magnet loses its strength if it is dropped repeatedly or heated. What is the safest way to store bar magnets?
options: In pairs with unlike poles together and wooden pieces between them
questions.explanation: Pairs arranged north to south with keepers help them stay magnetised.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Describe how a magnet can be used to separate iron nails from a mixture of nails and sand.
questions.answer: Move a magnet over the mixture. The iron nails stick to the magnet and the sand does not, so they are separated.
questions.explanation: Magnets can separate magnetic from non-magnetic materials.

questions.subject: science

questions.explanation: A potato is a swollen underground stem. Carrot, radish and beetroot are roots.

questions.subject: science

options: Honey lacks many nutrients such as proteins, vitamins and minerals in needed amounts
questions.explanation: Honey is mostly sugar, so a diet of only honey does not supply all nutrients.

questions.subject: science

questions.answer: A cow gives milk, a hen gives eggs and a honeybee gives honey.

questions.explanation: Many foods come from animals, such as milk, eggs, honey and meat.

questions.q: Explain why even a carnivore such as a lion depends indirectly on plants.
questions.answer: A lion eats animals such as deer, and the deer eat plants. If the plants were not there, the deer would have no food and the lion would have nothing to eat.
keyPoints: So the lion depends on plants indirectly
questions.explanation: Plants are the starting point of food for all living things.

questions.subject: science

questions.explanation: Carbohydrates and fats are the main energy-giving nutrients.

questions.explanation: Citrus fruits provide vitamin C, which prevents scurvy.

questions.answer: Fats give energy and keep the body warm. Sources are butter, ghee, oils and nuts.
questions.explanation: Fats provide more energy than the same amount of carbohydrates.

questions.answer: Washing after cutting and overcooking can destroy or wash out vitamins and minerals, so food loses nutritive value.
questions.explanation: Careful cooking preserves nutrients.

questions.subject: science

questions.explanation: Natural fibres come from plants and animals.

questions.subject: science

questions.answer: Jute is used to make gunny bags and ropes because the fibre is strong and coarse.
questions.explanation: The properties of a fibre decide its use.

options: Metals let heat pass easily to the food
questions.explanation: Metals are good conductors of heat.

questions.subject: science

questions.answer: Grouping makes it easier to study and use them. We can group them by appearance, hardness, solubility, or whether they float or sink.
questions.explanation: Materials with similar properties are placed together.

questions.subject: science

questions.answer: Add a spoonful of the material to a glass of water and stir well. If it disappears and the water looks uniform, it is soluble. If it stays as separate particles, it is insoluble.
questions.explanation: A fair test uses the same amount of water for each material.

questions.explanation: Cooling turns vapour into liquid, which is condensation.

options: Let it stand, pour off clear water, then filter
questions.explanation: Sedimentation and decantation remove most mud, and filtration removes the remaining fine particles.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is evaporation? Give one use of it.
questions.answer: Evaporation is the change of a liquid into vapour. It is used to get salt from sea water or to dry wet clothes.
questions.explanation: Evaporation leaves dissolved solids behind.

questions.q: A mixture contains chalk powder, iron filings and salt. Describe how to separate all three.
questions.answer: Use a magnet to remove the iron filings. Add water so salt dissolves and filter to remove chalk. Evaporate the filtrate to get salt.
questions.explanation: Choose each method according to the property of the substance.

questions.explanation: Evaporation or boiling changes a liquid into vapour.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Baking soda is added to vinegar and bubbles appear. Why is it said to be an irreversible change?
options: New substances are formed and cannot be turned back easily
questions.explanation: A gas is produced and new substances form, so the original ones are not recovered easily.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of these changes can be reversed?
questions.explanation: Salt can be recovered by evaporating the water.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A small gap is left between the rails of a railway track. Why?
options: Iron expands in summer and would bend the track without the gap
questions.explanation: Metals expand on heating, so gaps allow room for expansion.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is the making of curd from milk considered an irreversible change?
questions.answer: Curd has different properties from milk and the curd cannot be changed back into milk.
questions.explanation: A change in which a new substance forms permanently is irreversible.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A burning candle shows both reversible and irreversible changes. Explain.
questions.answer: Wax that melts near the flame and solidifies on cooling is a reversible change. The wax that burns gives new substances and cannot be recovered, which is irreversible.
questions.explanation: One event may include both types of change.

questions.explanation: Leaves take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen during photosynthesis.

questions.explanation: The ovary develops into a fruit, and the ovules into seeds.

options: It makes much less food, since leaves are the main food-making parts
questions.explanation: Leaves have chlorophyll and make food using sunlight.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Give two differences between tap root and fibrous root with one example of each.
questions.answer: A tap root has one main root with side branches (mango, gram). A fibrous root is a cluster of roots of similar size (wheat, grass).
questions.explanation: Root type is related to leaf venation.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Explain photosynthesis, mentioning raw materials and products.
questions.answer: In photosynthesis the leaf uses carbon dioxide and water, with sunlight and chlorophyll, to make food (starch/glucose) and release oxygen.
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis happens in green parts of the plant.

options: Muscles and tiny bristles that grip the ground
questions.explanation: Alternating contraction and relaxation of muscles and bristles help it to crawl.

questions.answer: Birds have light, hollow bones, strong chest muscles to flap the wings, and a streamlined body with feathers.
questions.explanation: Birds' bodies are suited to flight.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Compare the way a snake and a fish move.
questions.answer: A snake moves by making curves in the body and pushing against the ground using muscles and ribs. A fish pushes through water using its tail and fins with a streamlined body.
keyPoints: Fish uses tail and fins in water
questions.explanation: The surrounding decides the way of moving.

questions.explanation: A camel has long legs, a hump that stores fat and thick eyelashes, which suit desert life.

questions.q: Differentiate between terrestrial and aquatic habitats with one example each.
questions.answer: Terrestrial habitats are on land, such as forests and deserts. Aquatic habitats are in water, such as ponds and oceans.
questions.explanation: Habitats are broadly grouped as land or water.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A potted seedling placed near a window bends toward the light. Which characteristic of living things does this show?
questions.answer: It shows that living things respond to stimuli, here light, by changing the direction of growth.
questions.explanation: Plants respond to light, although they do not move from place to place.

questions.explanation: Periodic motion repeats itself at regular intervals.

questions.explanation: Length is the difference between two readings.

options: The Sun is low in the sky

questions.answer: Mirrors are used in dressing tables, as rear-view mirrors in vehicles and in barber shops.
questions.explanation: Mirrors reflect light to give images.

questions.answer: Clear glass is transparent so almost all light passes through, and very little light is blocked.
keyPoints: Little light blocked so no dark shadow

options: The filament of the bulb is broken (fused)
questions.explanation: A broken filament leaves a gap in the circuit so current cannot flow.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Differentiate a conductor from an insulator with two examples of each.
questions.answer: Conductors allow electricity to pass, such as copper and iron. Insulators do not, such as rubber and plastic.
questions.explanation: Metals are generally conductors.

questions.answer: Rubber and plastic are insulators, so they stop current from flowing through the tool to the electrician, which protects against shocks.
questions.explanation: Insulation provides safety.

questions.answer: Magnets are used in compass needles, refrigerator door seals and magnetic toys.

keyPoints: Animals eat plants or other animals
questions.explanation: All animals depend on plants directly or indirectly.

options: Chapati, dal, vegetables and a glass of milk

questions.q: Name the components of food and say which ones give us energy.
questions.answer: The components are carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, water and roughage. Carbohydrates and fats give energy.
questions.explanation: Each component has its own function.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why does a person doing heavy physical work need more energy-giving food than someone who sits at a desk?
questions.answer: Heavy work uses more energy, so the body needs more carbohydrates and fats to supply it.
questions.explanation: Energy needs depend on activity.

options: The fibre separates from the stalk more easily
questions.explanation: Soaking loosens the stems so that fibres can be peeled off.

questions.answer: Cotton absorbs sweat easily and lets it evaporate, so the body feels cool.

questions.answer: Ceramic and steel are strong, do not dissolve or soften in hot liquid, and can be used again and again.

Under the shade with no breeze

questions.explanation: Wool comes from animals.

questions.answer: Weaving uses two sets of yarn crossing at right angles and is done on a loom. Knitting uses a single yarn with needles.
keyPoints: Weaving: two sets of yarn at right angles
questions.explanation: Both turn yarn into fabric.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A person wants a warm jacket for a cold place. Which fibre will you suggest and why?
questions.answer: Wool, because the woollen fibres trap air which is a poor conductor of heat, keeping the body warm.
questions.explanation: The fibre is chosen according to its properties.

Wood is heavier for its size than iron

questions.explanation: Coins and paper clips are metallic and lustrous.

options: It sinks to the bottom as particles
It disappears and spreads evenly in the water
It changes the colour of the beaker

questions.subject: science

questions.answer: Hard: iron, stone. Soft: cotton wool, sponge.
questions.explanation: Hardness is a property we can test by pressing or scratching.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A cup of tea is stirred with a metal spoon and the handle becomes warm. Explain using a property of metals.
questions.answer: Metals allow heat to pass through them easily, so heat travels along the spoon from the hot tea to the handle.
questions.explanation: Metals are good conductors of heat.

questions.explanation: The magnet attracts the iron.

questions.explanation: Water evaporates but the salt remains.

questions.explanation: Rusting is a chemical change, not a separation method.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How does a farmer separate wheat grains from the husk?
questions.answer: By winnowing: the mixture is dropped from a height in the wind, so lighter husk blows away and grains fall in a heap.
questions.explanation: Weight difference allows separation.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why can't we use a sieve to separate salt from salt water but can use evaporation?
questions.answer: Dissolved salt particles are too small and pass through any sieve. Heating evaporates the water and leaves the salt.
questions.explanation: The method depends on the properties of the mixture.

questions.explanation: Cooked vegetables cannot be turned back to raw.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which change is caused by cooling?
questions.explanation: Water freezes when cooled.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A wet iron nail is left in the open for a week and becomes covered by a reddish-brown layer. Which statement is correct?
options: The nail has undergone a reversible change
The nail has undergone rusting, which is an irreversible change
questions.explanation: Rusting forms a new substance and cannot be reversed.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of these is a natural change?
questions.explanation: Day and night are natural changes that no one controls.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: List two ways to prevent rusting of iron articles.
questions.answer: Painting the iron or coating it with oil or grease keeps air and water away, preventing rust.
questions.explanation: Rust needs air and water.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why are the changes of a baked cake irreversible while melting of ice is reversible?
questions.answer: Baking forms new substances with new properties that cannot be turned back, but melting is only a change of state and the water can be frozen again.
questions.explanation: Reversibility depends on whether new substances form.

options: Wilt because it cannot take water from the soil
questions.explanation: Roots absorb water and minerals, so without them the plant wilts.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What are the functions of the stem?
questions.answer: The stem supports the plant, carries water and minerals from roots to leaves and carries food from leaves to other parts.
questions.explanation: The stem connects all parts.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Explain why most plants die if kept in dark for a long time.
questions.answer: Photosynthesis needs sunlight, so in the dark leaves cannot make food and the plant slowly starves.
questions.explanation: Light is essential for food making in green plants.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Bones are joined to muscles. When muscles contract they
options: Pull the bones and cause movement
questions.explanation: Muscles pull on bones to move them.

questions.subject: science

questions.explanation: The spinal cord runs inside the backbone.

questions.explanation: Muscles and tiny bristles grip the soil.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which statement correctly explains why we can swing our arms in circles but cannot rotate our knees in the same way?
options: The shoulder is a ball and socket joint, the knee is a hinge joint
questions.explanation: A ball and socket joint allows rotation, while a hinge joint allows movement in one direction.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which bones form the rib cage along with the chest bone?
questions.explanation: Ribs are curved bones that join the chest bone and the backbone.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why do birds have light bones, and how does the shape of a fish help it to swim?
questions.answer: Light bones make a bird's body light for flying. The streamlined shape of a fish reduces resistance of water.
questions.explanation: Body structure suits the way of moving.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What would happen if there were no muscles attached to our bones?
questions.answer: The bones could not be moved, so we could not walk, lift or bend, since muscles pull on bones.
questions.explanation: Movement needs both bones and muscles.

questions.subject: science

questions.explanation: Plants make their own food, but all living things need food.

questions.explanation: Forests are on land.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which feature helps a bird fly?
questions.explanation: Wings and feathers help birds to fly.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why do the leaves of many desert plants look small or spiny?
questions.explanation: Smaller leaves lose less water by transpiration.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The process of getting rid of waste by living organisms is called
questions.explanation: Excretion removes waste from the body.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Write any three differences between living and non-living things.
questions.answer: Living things grow, breathe, need food and reproduce, while non-living things do not.
questions.explanation: These are signs of life.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why are some animals active at night in the desert?
questions.answer: The days are very hot, so staying hidden in the day and coming out at night helps them save water and avoid heat.
questions.explanation: This is a habit that helps survival.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why should the eye be placed directly above the mark while reading a ruler?
questions.answer: Reading from the side gives a wrong value due to the slanted line of sight, so we must look straight at the mark.
questions.explanation: This avoids reading error.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A bus travels 36 km in a trip. Express the distance in metres and explain which unit is more convenient.
questions.answer: 36 x 1000 = 36000 m. Kilometre is more convenient since the number is smaller for long distances.
questions.explanation: Choose a unit that suits the size.

questions.explanation: An opaque object blocks light to form a shadow.

questions.explanation: The Sun is natural; the others are man-made.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In which case will the shadow of a ball be the biggest?
options: Ball far from lamp, near screen
Ball near lamp, far from screen
questions.explanation: The closer to the light and farther from the screen, the larger the shadow.

questions.explanation: The Moon reflects the Sun's light.

questions.answer: A mirror has a smooth shiny surface that reflects most light to form a clear image, but wood is rough and scatters light.
keyPoints: Wood does not form clear image
questions.explanation: Smooth polished surfaces give images.

questions.q: Explain why you see an upside-down image on a pinhole camera screen.
questions.answer: Light travels in straight lines, so rays from the top of the object go downward through the hole and rays from the bottom go upward, inverting the image.
questions.explanation: The crossing of rays inverts the image.

questions.explanation: A switch controls the circuit.

questions.subject: science

questions.answer: Copper is a metal and conducts electricity, while plastic is an insulator.
questions.explanation: Metals are good conductors.

questions.answer: Plastic is an insulator, so it prevents current passing to the electrician's hand and avoids shocks.
questions.explanation: Safety around live wires.
